uncited: This family adapts 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) for X-ray imaging and radiative physics by replacing view-dependent color with view-independent scalar attributes (density or intensity) .

It solves the problem of reconstructing volumetric density fields or synthesizing X-ray projections from 2D attenuation measurements, where physical attenuation depends on integrated density along the ray path rather than surface appearance .
All extensions in this family retain the core 3DGS primitive representation: a set of $M$ anisotropic 3D Gaussian kernels $\mathcal{G} = \{G_i\}_{i=1}^M$ .
In radiative and domain-specific variants, this is replaced by view-independent scalar attributes or feature vectors .
Radiative Gaussian Splatting introduced the concept of replacing RGB with scalar density for CT reconstruction .
X-Gaussian extended this to novel view synthesis and sparse-view reconstruction, highlighting performance advantages over NeRF-based methods .
The Radiative Gaussian Point Cloud Model further refined the attribute representation using a Radiation Intensity Response Function to avoid spherical harmonics .
Volumetric Primitives Radiance Field represents a divergence towards ray-primitive intersection methods for radiance field rendering .
